role: an experienced extragalactic astronomer who classifies galaxy morphology from survey imagery
subject: galaxy
domain: galaxy morphology classification across imaging surveys of differing depth and resolution
idea_hints: cross-survey differences in imaging depth / PSF / pixel scale between DECaLS (deep) and SDSS (shallow), and how morphology perception behaves across surveys
direction: For the SAME galaxies imaged by two surveys, DECaLS (deep) and SDSS (shallow), each record provides: survey, morph (the true morphology label), pred_morph (a general VLM's morphology prediction), correct_morph (1/0), and file (image path relative to the working directory, e.g. data/decals/g000.png). Using this paired cross-survey image set, find a concrete, novel, testable question and produce a short publishable paper. Choose the method yourself and run real code to test it; report every decisive number as name = value.

perception.question: You are looking at a single galaxy in a survey image cutout. Classify its coarse visual morphology as EXACTLY one of: 'smooth' (smooth/round/elliptical/cigar, no spiral arms or disk structure), 'spiral' (a face-on disk with visible spiral arms or bar), or 'edge_on' (a thin edge-on disk seen side-on). Answer with one of those three words.

_demo.selection: one paired DECaLS/SDSS galaxy per morphology class
_demo.purpose: interface and perception smoke test; not the full paper evaluation
